bullets.lead: Took a booking and payments platform from idea to production in 15 months:

bullets.rest: (public site, admin calendar, waitlist) so they can never disagree about a free slot; a constant 5 queries per month view, pinned by tests; published on GitHub.

bullets.lead: Eliminated double bookings under concurrent load:
bullets.rest: reproduced the race with a k6 load test, then serialized all five booking write paths with PostgreSQL advisory locks keyed per branch and day.

bullets.lead: Made Stripe payments safe to retry:
bullets.rest: Connect, Billing and Terminal (card readers, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android) with replay-safe webhooks and exactly-once guards, so a duplicate event cannot charge twice.

bullets.lead: Cut the booking-flow read from nine sequential queries to one
bullets.rest: (about 0.8 s cold before) with request-scoped memoization and a commit-invalidated cache; query-budget tests fail the build if the count grows.

bullets.lead: Made tenant isolation impossible to skip:
bullets.rest: an AST audit fails the test suite on any unguarded route, so a cross-tenant read cannot reach production; JWT with revocation, TOTP, passkeys and RBAC.

bullets.lead: Replaced review-time policing with 22 custom build guards
bullets.rest: that fail the build on secrets in logs, schema/migration drift, error-contract violations and stale documentation, so a standard cannot be broken silently.

bullets.lead: Built the test infrastructure behind 8,500+ automated tests
bullets.rest: (pytest on real PostgreSQL with an isolated database per run, Vitest, Playwright at desktop, phone and iOS-WebKit sizes with axe checks), so every release ships from green.

bullets.lead: Run production:
bullets.rest: blocking pre-deploy migrations, a full staging mirror, nightly off-platform backups with a verified restore, and Sentry keyed by commit, so every change is rehearsed on staging and every backup is known to restore.

bullets.lead: Collapsed eleven hand-rolled send loops into one notification module
bullets.rest: covering email, SMS, WhatsApp (34 Meta-approved templates) and push (APNs, FCM), so every message goes through the same policy and executor.

bullets.lead: Shipped the iOS and Android apps from the same React codebase
bullets.rest: through Capacitor, with native Tap to Pay, push notifications, passkeys and barcode scanning, so one codebase serves three clients.

bullets.lead: Ran several AI coding agents concurrently on one codebase
bullets.rest: and kept it safe by governing them with a 650-line standards document, 76 dated architecture decisions, a claim log, a pre-push hook and machine-checked invariants.

bullets.lead: Delivered the investor-facing website end to end
bullets.rest: with the founding team, from content structure to the live domain.

projects.title: Flagdown
projects.subtitle: Full-stack ride-sharing app in Go microservices and Next.js
projects.stack: Go, gRPC, RabbitMQ, Kafka, Redis, MongoDB, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Next.js

bullets.lead: Built five Go microservices and a Next.js front end on Kubernetes,
bullets.rest: with gRPC where the caller needs an answer, RabbitMQ where it only needs to announce an event, and WebSockets for live rider and driver updates.

bullets.lead: Made the driver service stateless
bullets.rest: by streaming positions through Kafka (keyed by driver ID) into an idempotent consumer that keeps a Redis geo index, so nearest-driver matching is one GEOSEARCH on any replica.

bullets.lead: Made message handling crash-safe:
bullets.rest: durable queues, acks after the work, backoff retries, dead-lettering and idempotent handlers, verified by a chaos test that kills a pod mid-ride and asserts no double-processing.

bullets.lead: Made every ride traceable end to end:
bullets.rest: Prometheus metrics and a provisioned Grafana dashboard on every service, with OpenTelemetry context carried through gRPC metadata and RabbitMQ headers.

bullets.lead: Built a live operations map
bullets.rest: (MapLibre GL, deck.gl) with streaming driver positions, an H3 demand heatmap and trip replay by seeking the Kafka log by timestamp, fed by a fleet simulator on OSRM routes.
